chunks: What the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted strengthen him — reported to me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
"The kurr of water that nothing can render impure is one thousand and two hundred raṭls."

As for the narrations that have been transmitted containing the specification by three spans, two cubits, and the like — there is no contradiction between them and what we have narrated, because it is not impossible that what has those dimensions should weigh one thousand and two hundred raṭls. And I will present some of the narrations that contain mention of that — and from them [is the following].

key_terms.التَّحْدِيدَ: delimitation, specification of a legal threshold
key_terms.الْكُرُّ: kurr — minimum volume of water immune to ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: What is the weight of a kurr of water according to Imam al-Ṣādiq in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq (AS) establishes the jurisprudential threshold called the kurr — the minimum volume of water that cannot be rendered ritually impure by any contaminant — as 1,200 raṭls (a unit of weight). Shaykh al-Ṭūsī appends a conciliatory juristic note, arguing that this weight-based definition does not contradict other narrations that specify the kurr in linear measures (spans and cubits), since a body of water with those dimensions would correspond to the same weight.
